articles.title: Narcissism and psychopathy are closely linked in women serving prison sentences
articles.summary: A recent study of 344 incarcerated adults reveals that narcissistic traits fuel psychopathic tendencies through calculating, manipulative behavior. The research highlights how dark personality traits blend into survival tactics behind bars, particularly among women.

articles.title: People shift their political opinions to match the room in small group chats
articles.summary: When politics comes up in small group chats, people often adjust their stated opinions to match the dominant viewpoint. New research using AI-simulated conversations reveals that social pressure can easily sway how we express our political beliefs.

articles.title: Parents of transgender youth faced declining mental health after the 2025 inauguration
articles.summary: A recent study reveals that parents of transgender youth experienced worsening mental health and heightened anxiety following the 2025 presidential inauguration. The research highlights the immediate emotional toll that shifting political climates take on families.

articles.title: Salsa dancing can ease depressive symptoms in young adults, randomized trial finds
articles.summary: Young adults experiencing depression and social anxiety might benefit from learning how to salsa dance. A new study indicates that an eight-week salsa program significantly reduced depressive symptoms and boosted daily happiness.

articles.title: Scientists say this simple habit could strengthen your marriage
articles.summary: Couples who exercise together report better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress than those who work out alone. Even something as simple as taking a walk together may create valuable opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected.

articles.title: Vagus Nerve Stimulation Could Help New Skills Stick
articles.summary: Stimulating the vagus nerve after practice helped mice develop stronger long-term motor learning, revealing a potentially important window when the brain is still locking in a new skill. The effect was linked to rhythmic changes in brain blood vessels, hinting that body-to-brain signals may help prepare the brain for lasting change.

articles.summary: arXiv:2610.03872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are becoming increasingly capable of generating scientific code, but generating code is not the same as improving the algorithms behind it. For numerical solvers, execution feedback can expose poor performance, but rarely reveals its underlying cause and how to address it. We introduce Auto-Diagnosis and Skill Discovery (ADSD), a framework that links numerical diagnosis to reusable solver self-improvement. articles.title: Least Squares for Time Series Forecasting
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.03812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A time-series forecast is scored on a future value of the series. A representation loss that regresses the next latent, as in LeNEPA, is a different least-squares problem on the same bottleneck. We write both programs down. articles.title: Where Does Jagged Competence Come From?
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.03831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Capable systems often show jagged competence: low average error alongside failures on particular inputs. We ask where it comes from in a task built from two known layers. A lower layer A computes five per-slot sums from records; an upper layer B uses the slot-1 sum and a mode carried over from earlier boards to predict the next board's category, so B cannot be computed from the current A alone: B is a strict extension of A. We train small recurrent networks on B and measure, against exact ground truth, what they acquire of A. The central finding
